governing_intent: Perform a documentation-only PG-19 governance audit of EOS inheritance readiness for AlienIntent: identify the canonical EOS repository/revision, inventory and normalize EOS authority issues without promoting unresolved material, document that no EOS conformance baseline currently exists, withdraw the earlier candidate pin with provenance, and update the specified AlienIntent governance records consistently while preserving existing gate counts.
summary: The supplied work packet presents a cohesive governance/documentation task with clear authority boundaries, explicit constraints, reported repository baselines, and a defined stop condition for Founder-level decisions. The controlling condition supports READY: unresolved Founder decisions are not to be made in this work, but are to be identified and presented; authorized documentation corrections may be applied only where existing accepted EOS authority already permits them.
implementation_unknowns: The exact contents and locations of the PG-19 work-unit document and affected AlienIntent governance files must be inspected during implementation.
The complete EOS artifact inventory relevant to AlienIntent inheritance must be derived from the supplied EOS repository revision during the audit.
Which EOS inconsistencies are correctable under already accepted EOS authority versus which require Founder approval must be determined artifact-by-artifact from the accepted governance records.
The exact wording needed to preserve provenance while withdrawing the earlier candidate EOS pin must be selected in context of the existing FD-06, G31, gate report, and validation record text.
The implementer must verify that the 34-row matrix and the 2 PASS / 0 DEFERRED / 32 BLOCKED counts remain unchanged after documentation edits.
verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through repository diffs and document review: EOS audit inventory and normalization plan exist; only authorized EOS corrections, if any, are made with cited rules; Founder-required corrections are stopped and presented plainly; AlienIntent records state that no EOS conformance baseline exists and withdraw the candidate pin with provenance; FD-06, G31, gate report, and validation record are consistent; prohibited code/config/test/runtime changes are absent; and specified matrix counts are unchanged. One independent review verdict is meaningful because the work has a single governance outcome and explicit constraints, even though it spans two repositories.
material_risks: The audit could accidentally treat draft, scaffold, proposed, or review-pending EOS material as authoritative, violating the hard constraints.
The implementer could overstep by creating or implying an EOS repository-wide version identity without Founder approval.

The distinction between editorial corrections authorized by existing accepted EOS authority and semantic/governance corrections requiring Founder decision may be subtle and must be documented carefully.
Cross-repository documentation updates may become inconsistent if AlienIntent records and EOS audit findings are not updated together.
The supplied clean baselines, revisions, and artifact conditions are reported facts from the packet and still need normal implementation-time confirmation before editing.
next_action: Proceed with the PG-19 documentation/governance audit as a single work packet, beginning by opening the referenced PG-19 work-unit and the reported EOS/AlienIntent baselines, then produce the inventory and normalization plan before making only clearly authorized documentation corrections.
rationale: The task has a clear governing intent and explicit negative authority: no implementation work, no promotion of unresolved EOS material, no weakening governance, no push or external mutation, and no Founder-level decisions by the implementer. The remaining unknowns are implementation and audit-discovery questions, not material owner-intent gaps. The apparent Founder decision needs are already handled by the requested stop-and-present deliverable rather than blocking readiness. The work is cohesive because the EOS audit, normalization plan, AlienIntent no-baseline record, and FD-06/G31 updates all serve one governance determination about EOS conformance readiness.
